jobs.title: Principal Engineer - AI Security
jobs.excerpt: As a Principal Engineer in AI Security, you will define and lead Thrivent’s strategy for defending against emerging external AI-powered threats.
jobs.description:
As a Principal Engineer in AI Security, you will define and lead Thrivent’s strategy for defending against emerging external AI-powered threats. This role focuses on protecting the enterprise from adversarial AI capabilities, including automated vulnerability discovery, exploitation, and AI-driven attack campaigns. You will operate at the intersection of cyber defense, artificial intelligence, and enterprise architecture, translating rapidly evolving external threats into practical, scalable protections across the organization. This role requires deep technical expertise, strong systems thinking, and the ability to influence security strategy at the highest levels.

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

Designing Solutions

  • Apply expert-level knowledge of AI-driven threats, cyber defense, and enterprise security architecture to define and drive outcomes that protect the organization from emerging AI-powered attack vectors.
  • Create the enterprise strategy for defending against AI-enabled threats, including automated vulnerability discovery, exploitation, and adversarial AI techniques.
  • Establish architecture for detection, prevention, and response capabilities specific to generative AI threat patterns.
  • Define and implement security patterns and guardrails to enable safe and secure enterprise consumption of AI technologies.
  • Drive integration of AI threat detection and controls into existing cyber defense tooling and platforms.
  • Build threat models focused on generative AI attack patterns and emerging adversarial techniques.

Implementing Solutions

  • Use independent, critical thinking to translate evolving AI threat intelligence into scalable engineering controls and defensive capabilities.
  • Lead the development of detection and response mechanisms for AI-driven attacks across enterprise environments.
  • Design and implement telemetry strategies to identify anomalous behavior indicative of AI-enabled threats.
  • Partner with Cyber Defense teams to operationalize detections, response playbooks, and automation for AI-related incidents.
  • Prototype and evaluate defensive applications of AI to enhance detection, response, and security operations.
  • Develop architecturally significant components that advance the organization’s ability to defend against AI-driven adversaries.

Learning and Applying New Techniques

  • Lead research initiatives focused on emerging AI threat capabilities, adversarial AI techniques, and evolving attack methodologies.
  • Maintain deep expertise in industry frameworks such as OWASP LLM Top 10 and MITRE ATLAS.
  • Continuously evaluate and introduce modern security technologies and approaches to address AI-era risks.
  • Drive adoption of innovative defensive techniques across the organization to stay ahead of threat evolution.

Collaborating Within the Team

  • Provide deep technical expertise in AI security to solve complex, high-impact problems and remove critical technical roadblocks.
  • Partner with product owners and engineering teams to incorporate AI security requirements into technical designs and user stories.
  • Act as a technical leader in system design across teams, ensuring AI security considerations are embedded into broader architecture decisions.
  • Mentor engineers and elevate AI security capabilities within teams.

Collaborating Across Teams

  • Partner closely with Cyber Defense, IAM, and Application Security teams to integrate AI threat protections across the security ecosystem.
  • Promote adherence to enterprise security standards while extending them to address AI-specific risks.
  • Broker design and implementation of AI security controls across product teams to support strategic priorities.
  • Drive alignment across teams on detection engineering, telemetry, and response strategies for AI threats.

Collaborating Across the Organization

  • Influence senior leadership on AI risk posture, threat landscape evolution, and required investments in defensive capabilities.
  • Provide enterprise-wide guidance on AI security architecture, ensuring consistent and scalable protection strategies.
  • Represent the organization externally on AI security topics when appropriate (industry forums, partnerships, etc.).
  • Translate complex AI security risks into actionable insights for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Setting Product/Platform Technology Strategy

  • Define enterprise-level capabilities required to defend against AI-powered threats.
  • Shape the strategic direction for AI security across cyber defense, detection engineering, and secure AI adoption.
  • Provide subject matter expertise to guide platform and security investments related to AI risk mitigation.

Defining Engineering Standards/Patterns

  • Establish and promote engineering standards for AI security, including secure AI usage patterns and detection frameworks.
  • Collaborate across teams to ensure consistent application of AI security controls and design patterns.
  • Drive adoption of best practices for integrating AI threat protections into engineering workflows and platforms.

DevOps

  • Provide technical leadership in identifying and responding to AI-driven security incidents and emerging threats.
  • Introduce resilient and scalable technologies to improve detection and response capabilities for evolving attack patterns.
  • Evaluate and implement enhancements to CI/CD and operational pipelines to incorporate AI security controls.
  • Influence cross-functional teams to proactively address risks associated with AI-enabled development and deployment.

Selecting and Managing Technology Vendors

  • Provide technical expertise in evaluating AI security tools, detection platforms, and emerging defensive technologies.
  • Assess how vendor solutions align with enterprise strategy for defending against AI-driven threats.
  • Contribute to selection criteria for platforms that enhance AI security posture and detection capabilities.

Coaching Engineers

  • Mentor engineers in AI security concepts, threat modeling, and detection engineering.
  • Provide guidance on best practices for securing AI-enabled systems and defending against adversarial AI techniques.
  • Deliver training, workshops, and knowledge-sharing sessions to build AI security expertise across the organization.

Recruiting and Building Talent

  • Engage in the broader AI and security community to strengthen organizational expertise and visibility in AI security.
  • Support recruitment efforts to hire engineers with specialized skills in AI security and advanced cyber defense.
  • Model Thrivent’s leadership competencies: Model the Way, Rally the Team, and Deliver Outcomes.
  • Foster a culture of continuous improvement, innovation, and strong security practices aligned to evolving AI risks.

QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS:

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or related technical field, or equivalent work experience
  • 10+ years of experience in security engineering or related field
  • Proven experience defining and executing enterprise security strategy
  • Deep knowledge of modern threats, attack techniques, and detection engineering
  • Experience with threat modeling, incident response, and security operations
  • Demonstrated ability to influence both technical and executive stakeholders

Preferred:

  • Experience working with AI/ML systems and security implications
  • Knowledge of adversarial AI techniques and AI threat modeling
  • Experience with XDR, SIEM, and detection engineering practices
  • Familiarity with AI security frameworks (e.g., OWASP LLM Top 10, MITRE ATLAS)
  • Financial services industry experience

Creator Coordinator

Function: Creator Sourcing | Influencer & UGC Partnerships | Creator Operations
Reports to: Creator Operations Lead
Location: Remote
Job Type: Full-Time, Contractor
Seniority Level: Entry–Mid Level
Fee: $2,000 – $2,500 USD

The Role:

We’re looking for a Creator Coordinator to join one of the UK’s leading agencies and become the driving force behind our creator sourcing operation.

This role is responsible for building and managing a consistent pipeline of high-quality UGC creators across multiple client accounts. You’ll identify new creator talent, vet creators against our internal quality standards, coordinate creator onboarding, build relationships and ensure our wider team always has access to the right creators for every campaign.

If you’re highly organised, proactive and passionate about creators, this is an opportunity to build your career within one of the fastest-growing agencies.

About Soar Group

The Soar Group is one of the UK's fastest-growing performance agency groups, built around a specialist paid media core — with Meta as our primary growth channel — backed by an in-house creative execution arm and a dedicated TikTok Shop implementation capability.

With over £100M+ in annual ad spend under management and a team of 130+, we partner with ambitious 7-9 figure DTC and eCommerce brands, with Meta as our primary growth channel, alongside TikTok and Google.

Our capabilities include:

  • Performance Media – Full-funnel paid media and growth strategy across Meta, Google, and TikTok, with Meta as our primary growth channel.
  • Creative Execution – An in-house creative execution arm delivering high-production creative, UGC, and static content at scale.
  • TikTok Shop & Social Commerce – A dedicated TikTok Shop implementation and creator-led growth capability.

We were nominated for Meta's Creative Diversity Award 2025 and recognised by Meta as the UK's #1 independent Meta agency group.

Our culture is built around four core values: Extreme Ownership, Radical Curiosity, Kind Candour, Outcome Obsessed.

Requirements

Comprehensive training will be provided across all aspects of the role, including our creator sourcing processes, internal systems and creator ecosystem.

  • Launch UGC creator casting calls across in our creator community. Source externally on social media platforms to build a consistent pipeline of high-quality creators.
  • Source and identify creators that align with each client’s brand, audience and campaign objectives.
  • Vet and review UGC creators based on content quality, performance, audience fit and brand suitability to ensure only the strongest creators are recommended.
  • Maintain a curated, engaged creator network, ensuring all creators are contractually bound and compliant before any assignment begins.
  • Execute multi-platform creator outreach using tools including TikTok Creator Marketplace, Insense, X (formerly Twitter) and other relevant sourcing platforms.
  • Coordinate creator communications throughout the onboarding process, acting as a professional point of contact.
  • Support the wider team with administrative tasks, campaign coordination and creator operations.
  • Continuously identify opportunities to improve creator sourcing processes and expand the quality and scale of our creator network.
  • Act as an external ambassador for the agency in all creator-facing interactions, representing the agency with professionalism, empathy, and clarity. Strong creator relationships protect the agency's reputation, drive long-term partnerships, and reduce the risk of negative sentiment.
  • Maintain strong relationships internally and externally.

Who You Are:

We’re looking for someone who is organised, proactive and excited by the world of creator marketing. You don’t need years of experience-we’re looking for potential, curiosity and a willingness to learn.

You’ll ideally have:

  • 1+ years’ experience in influencer marketing, creator partnerships, social media, affiliate marketing or a related field.
  • A Strong understanding of social media (Meta, TikTok etc) and creator culture
  • Excellent organisational skills with exceptional attention to detail.
  • Strong written communication and relationship-building skills.
  • Confidence in managing multiple tasks and deadlines simultaneously.
  • A proactive mindset and willingness to take ownership.
  • The ability to work independently in a fast-paced remote environment.
  • A genuine interest in eCommerce, content creation and creator marketing.
  • Empathy, with a genuine ability to understand creator and client needs.
  • Creative thinking, with the ability to spot fresh ideas and creator talent.
  • Critical thinking, to evaluate creator quality and campaign fit with sound judgement.
  • Experience using TikTok Creator Marketplace and Meta Creator Marketplace.
  • Experience sourcing UGC creators or influencers.

Success in the first 6 months:

  • Built a reliable pipeline of high-quality creators across multiple industries.
  • Own creator briefing from start to finish.
  • Become a trusted partner to our team for creator sourcing and coordination.
  • Helped launch successful creator campaigns that generate measurable commercial results.
  • Build strong relationships with creators that lead to repeat collaborations and long-term partnerships.

Benefits

Benefits

  • 20 days annual leave.
  • Access to ongoing training, development, and progression opportunities across the Soar Group.

Soar Group is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment, where all of our employees have equal access to opportunities and everyone’s voices are heard. We respect and value all differences (seen and unseen) and strongly encourage applications from all backgrounds, which will be considered regardless of race, colour, religion or belief, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, pregnancy and maternity, disability, or age.

Due to the evolving nature of the business, the job holder may be required to carry out duties that are not detailed within this job description.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

As an AI Tutor specialized in multilingual audio capabilities, you will contribute to SpaceXAI's mission by training and refining Grok to excel in voice interactions, speech recognition, and auditory experiences across diverse languages, accents, and cultural contexts. Your work will focus on curating and annotating high-quality audio data to enhance Grok's global accessibility, enabling natural spoken interactions for users worldwide, bridging language barriers through accurate speech processing, and improving the AI's handling of multilingual audio nuances.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Use proprietary software to provide labels, annotations, recordings, and inputs on projects involving multilingual audio clips, voice recordings, speech samples, and auditory elements in various languages.
  • Translate and localize text strings (UI copy, prompts, responses, and other written content) from English into Slovenian, ensuring linguistic accuracy, natural phrasing, and cultural appropriateness.

  • Collaborate with technical staff to develop tasks that improve AI's ability to handle speech modulation, accent variation, noise in real-world recordings, and multilingual audio processing.
  • Work with technical staff to improve annotation tools for efficient audio workflows.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Native proficiency in Slovenian with exposure to diverse accents, dialects, or regional variations.
  • Proficiency in English (minimum B2 level) with clear, natural vocal delivery and pronunciation suitable for audio recording purposes.

  • Demonstrated ability to handle multilingual audio content, including evaluating speech accuracy, cultural vocal expressions, and contextual interpretation in spoken form.
  • Demonstrated ability to transcribe audio with high accuracy across accents and varying audio quality.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate and localize text accurately between English and Slovenian, preserving meaning, tone, and cultural nuance.
  • Comfort providing high-quality voice recordings and feedback on audio samples in multiple languages.
  • Strong comprehension skills and the ability to make independent judgments on ambiguous or varied audio material, including noisy or accented speech.
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, analytical, detail-oriented, and organizational skills, with the ability to articulate audio-related feedback effectively.
  • Commitment to developing AI that masters sophisticated multilingual audio capabilities.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Demonstration of exceptional attention to linguistic nuance, auditory detail, and data quality beyond standard transcription work.
  • Deep understanding and taste of what good/useful Audio data is.
  • Strong command of advanced transcription and annotation practices, including handling disfluencies, accents, and prosodic features (intonation, stress, rhythm, emotion, etc) with high consistency and accuracy.
  • Background in linguistics (e.g., phonetics, phonology, sociolinguistics), speech sciences, cognitive science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience, with demonstrated ability to analyze accent variation, pronunciation differences, and multilingual speech patterns.
  • Experience working with speech/audio datasets, annotation workflows, or AI training data, including knowledge/experience with training voice models, and an understanding of how data quality impacts model performance.
  • Experience with translation or localization workflows, particularly for software UI, product copy, or conversational AI text.
  • Professional experience in voice work, including voice acting, voice recording, podcasting with a measurable audience (e.g., X following), or similar audio production demonstrating attention to clarity and recording quality.
  • Demonstrated ability to exercise independent judgment in ambiguous audio scenarios and make consistent, defensible annotation decisions.
  • Portfolio (strongly preferred for advanced candidates): Voice samples, annotated transcripts, or audio-related work demonstrating quality, methodology, and attention to detail.
  • Candidates with professional experience in voice, linguistics, speech data, or speech evaluation and research are especially encouraged to apply.

LOCATION AND OTHER EXPECTATIONS:

  • Tutor roles may be offered as full-time, part-time, or contractor positions, depending on role needs and candidate fit.
  • For contractor positions, hours will vary widely based on project scope and contractor availability, with no fixed commitments required. Contractors have full flexibility to set their own hours and determine the exact amount of time needed to complete deliverables.

jobs.title: Key Account Manager E-Commerce CRM / E-Mail Marketing
jobs.excerpt: Wir wachsen schneller, als unsere Betreuungsstruktur mitkommt.
jobs.description:
Wir wachsen schneller, als unsere Betreuungsstruktur mitkommt. Aktuell hängen zu viele Entscheidungen an zu wenigen Köpfen — und unsere Account Manager:innen brauchen jemanden, der sie führt, nicht nur jemanden, der über ihnen steht.

Deshalb bauen wir die Ebene der Key Account Manager aus. Du übernimmst ein eigenes Team und ein eigenes Kundenportfolio — und gestaltest mit, wie Betreuung bei MAILODY in Zukunft funktioniert.

Wir sagen offen dazu: Diese Rolle ist gerade die anspruchsvollste im Unternehmen. Du bekommst Druck von oben (Wachstumsziele) und von unten (ein Team, das sich erst einspielt). Wir wissen das, wir lassen dich damit nicht allein — aber wir tun auch nicht so, als wäre es bequem.

Aufgaben

Führung

  • Du führst 3–5 Account Manager:innen fachlich und disziplinarisch.
  • Du führst wöchentliche 1:1s nach klarer Struktur (Fortschritt / Probleme / Pläne) und verantwortest die Gesundheit deines Teams.
  • Du entwickelst deine Leute aktiv weiter — Schulungen, Feedback, strukturierte Einarbeitung.

Kunden

  • Du verantwortest Entwicklung und Ergebnis deines eigenen Kundenportfolios (Richtwert 6–8 Accounts, ausschließlich unsere anspruchsvollsten Kunden). Das Tagesgeschäft liegt bei deinen AMs.
  • Du bist geschätzter Ansprechpartner auf der Senior-Entscheiderebene deiner Kunden und platzierst Themen aktiv in Kunden-Calls.
  • Du erkennst Churn-Risiken früh, entscheidest die Gegenmaßnahmen für dein Team und drehst gefährdete Accounts zurück in Wachstum.

Fachlichkeit & Prozesse

  • Du bist die fachliche Rückfallebene deines Teams — Klaviyo- und CRM-Architektur beherrschst du in der Breite.
  • Du coachst deine AMs fachlich und baust ihre Fähigkeiten auf, statt nur Fragen zu beantworten.
  • Du ownst einen unternehmensweiten Prozess rund um unsere Mitarbeitenden (z. B. Onboarding oder Offboarding).
  • Du stimmst Standards mit den anderen Key Account Managern ab und teilst Learnings aktiv.

Qualifikation

  1. Mindestens 3–4 Jahre Erfahrung im E-Mail-Marketing oder CRM; davon idealerweise ein Teil in einer Agentur oder im E-Commerce.
  2. Tiefe Praxis in Klaviyo oder einem vergleichbaren System (Braze, Emarsys, Bloomreach, Salesforce Marketing Cloud). Du hast komplexe Set-ups selbst gebaut, nicht nur begleitet.
  3. Erste Führungs- oder Mentoring-Erfahrung— du hast schon einmal Verantwortung für die Arbeit anderer getragen. Das muss nicht disziplinarisch gewesen sein.
  4. Sicherheit im Kundenkontakt auf Entscheiderebene— du hast schon mit Geschäftsführung oder Marketingleitung auf Augenhöhe gesprochen.
  5. Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau und gutes Englisch, schriftlich wie mündlich.
  6. Wohnsitz in Deutschland(steuer- und sozialversicherungsrechtlich zwingend).

Und was wir uns wünschen, aber nicht voraussetzen: Du gibst Feedback direkt und nimmst es genauso an. Du fragst nach dem Warum hinter den Zahlen eines Kunden. Du wartest nicht, bis dir jemand einen Prozess gibt.

Das ist nichts für dich, wenn …

  • … du Führung als Beförderung siehst und nicht als eigenes Handwerk, das man lernen muss.
  • … du Dinge lieber selbst machst, als sie abzugeben und jemanden dabei besser zu machen.
  • … du eine fertige Struktur erwartest. Wir bauen sie gerade — mit dir.
  • … du unangenehme Gespräche aufschiebst. Ein Teil dieser Rolle besteht daraus.
  • … du im Homeoffice Struktur von außen brauchst. Wir arbeiten vollständig remote.

Benefits

  • Ein Team, das dir gehört — und die Freiheit, es zu formen.
  • Klarheit über deinen eigenen Weg: Wir haben eine ausformulierte Level-Matrix. Du siehst schwarz auf weiß, was auf deinem Level erwartet wird und was der nächste Schritt ist.
  • Halbjährliche Entwicklungsgespräche mit echtem Feedback statt Formularen. Gehalt wird bei uns nach System vergeben, nicht nach Verhandlungsgeschick.
  • Führungskräfte-Ausbildung mit einem externen Coach, der Führungsteams bei Meta und in mehreren Scale-ups aufgebaut hat.
  • 100 % remote, überall in Deutschland — plus regelmäßige Team-Offsites und Workations.
  • MacBook, bei Bedarf zusätzliche Hardware.
  • 50 € monatliche Sachbezugskarte nach der Probezeit.

Sechs Sätze, an denen wir uns messen lassen — auch als Führungskraft:

Be confident.

We don't need all the answers to start, just the grit to find them first.

Be curious.

Let's be obsessed to find the ‚Why‘ to unlock the ‚How‘.

Keep growing.

Treat yourself like brilliant software: ship a new upgrade every month.

Be accountable.

Openness over cosiness. We own our words.

Act entrepreneurial.

Don't just do tasks: own real business impact.

Over-deliver where it matters.

Promise what's possible. Then challenge these boundaries.

Cisco SSE offers a comprehensive end-to-end zero trust access security portfolio including VPN, zero trust access, web inspection in the cloud, firewall as a service, CASB, DLP and more. Cisco SSE deployment flexibility allows customers to select solutions tailored to their needs and transition seamlessly as requirements evolve.

You work globally across regions and time zones in support of our largest and most strategic SSE customers, coordinating with globally distributed engineering teams. Expect participation in a follow-the-sun escalation model and significant travel to customer sites and engineering hubs.

Serve as the technical liaison between Cisco SSE product management and engineering and our largest, most strategic enterprise SSE customers! Represent the product organization to customers by clearly recommending deployment best practices, issue findings, root causes, workarounds, product constraints, and delivery timelines. Represent the customer within the product organization by bringing production context, business impact, operational constraints, and technical requirements into build and prioritization discussions. Own sophisticated escalations, balancing realistic customer expectations with accurate, reproducible technical evidence while advocating for outcomes that protect customer environments. Translate requirements, RCAs, and technical decisions between customer and engineering contexts without losing fidelity on either side.

Frontend and Product Integration

Through compassionate, individualized care,a culture focused on compliance and ethics, supportive user-centric technology, and customized financial solutions, we've helped over 1 million clients on their path to a brighter future.

While we're proud of what we've already accomplished, we're searching for new collaborators to help us get to the next level! If you're looking to join a forward-thinking, rapidly growing organization with helping people as its number one goal, we want to hear from you.

Role Overview

As our Staff Application Security Engineer, you will be the primary owner and driver of our application security program. You'll work hands-on with engineering teams to embed secure development practices, improve tooling and automation, and guide security considerations for new features, architectures, and services.

This is a high-impact role where you'll shape the future of AppSec at a company that values security as a core part of product quality.

What You'll Do

Application Security Ownership

  • Lead and evolve the company's application security strategy, roadmap, and day-to-day operations.
  • Serve as the primary AppSec partner for numerous dev teams working on Ruby on Rails web apps, React Native mobile apps, and various other projects including Python and Go.
  • Provide security guidance during design, development, and code review for new features and projects.
  • Drive adoption of secure coding practices and threat-modeling across engineering teams.

Tooling & Automation

  • Manage and optimize existing AppSec tooling, including:
  • GitHub Advanced Security (SAST, SCA, Secret Scanning)
  • Invicti (DAST)
  • Hadrian (ASM)
  • AppDome (mobile application security)
  • Cloudflare WAF
  • Improve automation and integration of security tools into CI/CD pipelines.
  • Identify and implement additional tools or processes to strengthen the security posture.

Secure SDLC & Developer Enablement

  • Build and maintain secure development standards, playbooks, and training materials.
  • Partner with engineering teams during sprint planning and feature design to proactively address risks.
  • Conduct security reviews, code assessments, and vulnerability triage with development teams.

Cloud & DevOps Collaboration

  • Work with DevOps to ensure secure AWS infrastructure deployments and configurations.
  • Contribute to hardening efforts across ECS, IAM, networking, and supporting cloud services.
  • Assist in designing and maintaining secure CI/CD workflows.

Incident & Vulnerability Management

  • Lead or support investigation and remediation of application-level vulnerabilities.
  • Monitor, prioritize, and track findings from SAST/DAST/ASM tools.
  • Collaborate with engineering to ensure timely and effective remediation.

What We're Looking For

Required Skills & Experience

  • 8+ years of experience in Application Security, Product Security, or related engineering roles.
  • Strong understanding of secure coding practices, common vulnerabilities (OWASP Top 10), and modern SDLC.
  • Experience working with cloud-native applications, ideally in AWS.
  • Understanding of SSL certificates & cryptographic key management.
  • Hands-on experience with SAST, DAST, WAFs, and/or mobile application security tools.
  • Ability to partner effectively with developers and influence secure design decisions.
  • Familiarity with GitHub-based workflows and CI/CD pipelines.

Nice to Have

  • Development experience with Ruby on Rails or similar dynamic languages.
  • Knowledge of AWS ECS/EKS, container security, secrets management and infrastructure-as-code (CloudFormation, Terraform).
  • Experience building or maturing an AppSec program from early stages.
  • SOAR Automation & Scripting experience.
  • Experience working in a PCI-compliant environment working with annual reporting needs.

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate measures success by reduced risk, not tickets closed, and reaches for secure design and simple guardrails before another scanner or gate. They think like an attacker but bring a developer mindset to their partnership with engineering, connecting the dots across application code, cloud infrastructure, and the pipeline rather than treating each as a separate domain. Engineers trust their technical judgment beyond the systems they personally own: they catch a bad design before it ships even when it isn't theirs, and they see a blocker coming early enough to design around it instead of just navigating it well after the fact.

While you make a difference for others, we’ll work to make a difference for you, providing an uplifting, collaborative work environment and benefits that reflect your value to us. For eligible full-time employees, we offer:

  • Considerable employer contributions for health, dental, and vision programs

About ShareGate

ShareGate is the leading Microsoft 365 migration and governance platform, trusted by over 100,000 IT pros for its unmatched simplicity.

It offers the simplest, most reliable, and most affordable way to move business data to Microsoft 365.

Whether migrating from Google Workspace, file shares, Exchange Online, SharePoint On-Premises, or tenant-to-tenant, ShareGate gets the job done, without surprises. From cloud transformation to M&A integration, it keeps things just damn simple.

ShareGate also helps organizations stay in control once their data is migrated. Its powerful governance features let users assess environments, uncover issues, and apply fixes on the spot, so everything stays clean, secure, and optimized. It lays the groundwork for safe Microsoft Copilot deployment within organizations.

ShareGate is developed by Workleap Technologies, a Montréal‑based software company.

Your role

ShareGate's Account Management team owns renewals and expansion across our existing customer base and the motion is about to change. Today it runs fast and transactional: a large book, short cycles, high volume. Where we're headed is more deliberate: a segmented renewal motion with real cross-sell revenue built into it. As Manager, Account Management, you own that transition and the team that delivers it.

You'll lead 4–8 Account Managers accountable for GRR, NRR, and expansion. You'll coach on live deals, rebuild the playbook as you go, and stay close enough to the pipeline to know what's actually happening in it. Leading through change means owning the friction your team runs into and being straight with them about what's shifting and why.

This is a builder’s role. If you've run a high-velocity renewal motion and know what it takes to turn it into an expansion engine, this one's for you.

Your impact:

  • Hit team-level targets across GRR, NRR, and expansion by running a proactive, structured renewal motion instead of reacting at T-90;
  • Transform a high-velocity renewal team into a segmented, expansion-led one, sequencing the change so throughput holds while the new motion takes root;
  • Grow cross-sell revenue by leading the ShareGate Protect motion into the existing Migrate base and coaching AMs to open second-product conversations that actually land;
  • Develop a team of 4–8 Account Managers through weekly 1:1s, pipeline reviews, and live deal coaching that builds skill, not just tracks numbers;
  • Protect revenue at risk by surfacing churn signals early, coaching save plays, and escalating before a renewal becomes a rescue;
  • Deliver forecasts leadership can trust, holding the bar on HubSpot pipeline hygiene and using AI to turn CRM data into decisions rather than reports;
  • Remove friction across the renewal and expansion cycle by partnering with RevOps, Channel, Finance, and Legal on segmentation, reporting, and capacity planning.

Your team

You'll report to the Director, Account Management and inherit a segment of an established team — people who know the book, the customers, and where the current motion strains. Your first job is earning their trust; your second is changing how they work without breaking what already performs.

You'll work closely with Channel, RevOps, Finance, Legal, and HR, and you'll lean on Sales Enablement and Product Marketing to give your team the positioning and talk tracks that make cross-sell conversations feel natural rather than bolted on. The leaders who do best here over-communicate and stay organized, especially when the answer isn't settled yet.

What you'll bring

  • 2+ years leading an Account Management or Customer Success function accountable for both renewal and expansion targets, with a track record of hitting them;
  • Experience across both ends of the motion — high-velocity transactional renewals and white-glove, strategic accounts — and the judgment to know which one an account needs;
  • A builder's instinct: you make bets, find out fast whether they worked, and change course in front of your team without losing them;
  • Strong leadership through change: you over-communicate, own the frustrations your team hits, and stay honest when the answer isn't clear yet;
  • Strong coaching instincts and radical candor: you can watch a call, name the moment it went sideways, and explain it in a way that sticks;
  • Working AI fluency: you build workflows and use AI to analyze CRM data and pressure-test decisions, not just to draft emails (HubSpot experience is a plus);
  • Bonus: familiarity with the Microsoft 365 ecosystem, or experience taking a velocity-driven team through the shift to expansion-led.

Most of this sounds like you? Apply.

What the job comes with

    • Pay mix: 65% base salary, 35% variable

  • Remote work, with access to our Montreal office.

What drives us

We build software that sits at the center of how people experience work, every day, at every level.

We move fast. Priorities shift, decisions get made with the information we have, and we iterate. If you thrive on intensity and ambiguity doesn't slow you down, you'll feel right at home.
We're builders. We do what it takes to move forward. AI is part of our toolkit. We use it to go faster and decide smarter, not to replace judgment.

If you want real impact and a place where your decisions matter, this is it.

How we hire

Transparency is how we hire — for you as much as for us.

Here's how it works: a first call with a recruiter, then a virtual interview with the hiring manager. You'll then complete a take-home case study, followed by a meet with future colleagues to discuss it together. Depending on the role, the process may vary slightly — your recruiter will walk you through it on your first call.

jobs.description:
Global Head of Customer Experience

Reporting Line

Reports directly to the Group CEO. Senior leadership role with dozens of direct and indirect reports across customer-facing functions.

Location

Fully remote. Candidates based in or near one of our hubs — Dubai, Kuala Lumpur, Limassol, or Bangkok — are strongly preferred. Occasional travel to company locations and key markets. No relocation requirement.

General Purpose

This is one of the broadest CX mandates in multi-asset brokerage: ownership of every client touchpoint across forex, crypto, prop trading, prediction markets, and education, with a direct line to the Group CEO and dozens of people behind you. The role exists to turn that scale into a structural advantage — building a single, coherent client experience where today there are fragmented journeys, and making that experience the reason clients choose us and stay.

Like most brokers, our client functions have grown in silos — onboarding, support, retention, and product experience each doing their own thing, with no shared logic and no single owner. That's the problem this role was created to fix.

The candidate who thrives here won't be managing a tidy function; they'll be the first person to own the full picture, with the seniority and remit to actually change it.

The competitive bet is specific: in a market where most multi-asset brokers compete on price and acquisition, we intend to win on retention and trust. This role is how we do that.

Specific Objectives

Phase 1 — Diagnose (days 1–90)

The firm knows exactly where its client experience is broken

Within 90 days, a rigorous, evidence-based assessment exists across all products and touchpoints — forex, crypto, prop trading, prediction markets, and education — with gaps, friction points, and churn drivers named by root cause. This is the gate. Nothing in Phase 2 is possible without it. The audit will require navigating entrenched team boundaries and producing findings that are acted on, not shelved.

Phase 2 — Build (months 3–9)

Clients get support that's measurably better than the market

Support performance across all business lines sits consistently in the top quartile vs. a regularly updated competitive benchmark — measured across response time, first-contact resolution, self-service adoption, and automation coverage, including modern AI tools.

The firm's highest-value clients stay and spend more

A structured VIP programme is running — dedicated coverage, proactive engagement, retention workflows — with double-digit churn reduction in the VIP segment by month 12.

The function scales with the business, not against it

Operating models, tooling, and governance exist that let the function grow with both client volume and new product lines without headcount growing proportionally. The numerical drivers of CX capacity are defined, and technology delivers measurable year-on-year reduction in human labor per client interaction.

Experience failures are caught and contained before they hurt the business

Tiered CX SLOs are defined across all critical client journeys — trading execution and funding at the tightest thresholds, onboarding and support at appropriate levels. The toil ratio — the share of CX incidents requiring human intervention vs. automated resolution — falls year-on-year as automation matures.

Phase 3 — Commercialise (months 9–12)

CX is a quantifiable business driver, not a cost centre

By month 12, there's a clear, evidenced link between CX improvements and business outcomes: conversion rates, trading volume, retention, and referrals. End-to-end analytics — predictive and prescriptive — turn client data into forward-looking decisions, not backward-looking reports.

Key Activities

Run a structured CX audit

Map every client touchpoint across forex, crypto, prop trading, prediction markets, and education — talk to internal stakeholders, dig into support data, and produce a prioritised gap assessment that names friction points and churn drivers by root cause.

Design the CX operating model

Build the governance structure, team ownership, and process logic that brings previously siloed functions — onboarding, support, retention, product experience — under a single framework. Own the architecture decisions and drive adoption across the organisation.

Run and improve support operations

Manage day-to-day support performance across all business lines, with targets set against a live competitive benchmark. Lead deployment of AI-powered tools and automation to drive step-change improvements, not incremental ones.

Build the VIP client programme

Design the coverage model for high-value clients — dedicated relationship management, proactive engagement, retention workflows — and own the commercial outcomes for this segment against double-digit churn reduction targets.

Make CX operations scale

Design operating models, tooling, and governance that grow with client volume and new product lines without proportional headcount growth. Define the numerical drivers of CX capacity and implement technology that delivers measurable year-on-year efficiency gains.

Deploy CX health monitoring

Build automated systems that track client experience in real time. Define tiered CX SLOs calibrated to journey criticality — tightest thresholds for trading execution and funding, appropriate levels for onboarding and support. Drive the toil ratio down year-on-year, with self-healing where possible and clean escalation where not.

Align the organisation around CX outcomes

Work with product, marketing, compliance, and commercial teams to embed client experience logic into roadmap decisions, campaign design, and new product launches — so CX is a design input, not a post-launch fix.

Measure and report CX as a commercial driver

Own the analytics framework — predictive and prescriptive — that connects CX performance to business outcomes: conversion, trading volume, retention, and referrals. Report at leadership level and use it to drive decisions, not just describe the past.

Key Competences

CX architecture and operating model design

Able to design governance structures, team ownership models, and process logic from scratch — not just optimise an existing function. Relevant here because there is no inherited architecture: the operating model needs to be built from zero across five distinct business lines.

Data and analytics fluency

Comfortable with predictive and prescriptive analytics, CX SLO frameworks, and using client data to drive forward-looking commercial decisions. Relevant because the commercial driver objective requires a direct, evidenced linkage between CX performance and business outcomes.

AI and automation literacy

Practical experience deploying AI-powered support tools, self-service systems, and automated monitoring — enough to make credible build/buy/partner decisions and hold vendors accountable. Relevant because support performance and health monitoring both depend on technology choices made early in the mandate.

Commercial acumen

Able to connect CX performance directly to business outcomes — conversion, retention, trading volume, referrals — and present that linkage credibly at Group CEO and board level. Relevant because this role is explicitly accountable for CX as a revenue driver, not a cost centre.

Cross-functional influence

Track record of bringing product, marketing, compliance, and commercial teams around CX outcomes without direct authority. Relevant because the siloed functions this role consolidates did not previously share a single owner — credibility will need to be built, not assumed.

Leading large, distributed teams

Experience managing dozens of direct and indirect reports across multiple functions and geographies, including through significant organisational change. Relevant because the span of control is immediate and consolidation of previously independent teams will require sustained leadership through transition.

Likely Current Job

Head of CX / VP Customer Experience at a retail broker or fintech

The most direct feeder — someone running an established CX function at a forex, crypto, or multi-product trading platform who's ready for a greenfield mandate with broader scope.

Chief Experience Officer at a mid-size regulated financial services firm

A step-up candidate who has owned the full client lifecycle at a smaller firm and is ready for a more complex, multi-asset environment.

Head of Operations at a retail broker (transition hire)

Adjacent role — someone who has managed scale and process efficiency and is deliberately moving toward owning the client experience end-to-end. Has the operational credibility; the CX ownership is the intentional next step, not an assumed natural fit.

Senior CX leader at a high-growth payments or digital banking firm

Transferable context — regulated, retail-facing, high transaction volume, automation-heavy. May lack trading-specific knowledge but brings strong architecture and analytics credentials.

Global Support / Service Delivery Director at a multi-product financial platform

Feeder from the support side — has managed large distributed teams and automation programmes, ready to step up to full CX ownership.

Employer Value Proposition

The broadest CX canvas in multi-asset brokerage

Most CX leadership roles sit inside one product line. This one spans forex, crypto, prop trading, prediction markets, and education — five distinct client journeys in a single mandate. The complexity is real and the scope is rare.

Global scale as a design constraint

This is not a single-market role. The function spans multiple geographies and cultures, which means the operating model, team management, and experience design all have to work across meaningfully different contexts. A harder and more interesting problem than running a regional function.

A direct line to commercial outcomes

The mandate is explicit: CX is a business driver, not a cost centre. You will be expected to show the link between experience improvements and conversion, retention, trading volume, and referrals — and you will have the seniority and access to move those numbers.

Real strategic autonomy at Group CEO level

Reports directly to the Group CEO with a genuine mandate to set the CX model from scratch — not inherit someone else's architecture or execute a pre-determined strategy. The Group CEO is sponsor and sounding board, not the person making the design decisions.

No playbook, no prior owner, and teams that didn't ask for a unified boss

There is no inherited framework. The siloed teams you'll be consolidating have operated independently until now, and building credibility across them will require influence without full positional authority.

Compensation

Competitive base salary plus performance-based bonus. Standard employee benefits apply.

jobs.title: Teamleiter CRM / E-Mail Marketing
jobs.excerpt: Wir wachsen schneller, als unsere Betreuungsstruktur mitkommt.
jobs.description:
Wir wachsen schneller, als unsere Betreuungsstruktur mitkommt. Aktuell hängen zu viele Entscheidungen an zu wenigen Köpfen — und unsere Account Manager:innen brauchen jemanden, der sie führt, nicht nur jemanden, der über ihnen steht.

Deshalb bauen wir die Ebene der Key Account Manager aus. Du übernimmst ein eigenes Team und ein eigenes Kundenportfolio — und gestaltest mit, wie Betreuung bei MAILODY in Zukunft funktioniert.

Wir sagen offen dazu: Diese Rolle ist gerade die anspruchsvollste im Unternehmen. Du bekommst Druck von oben (Wachstumsziele) und von unten (ein Team, das sich erst einspielt). Wir wissen das, wir lassen dich damit nicht allein — aber wir tun auch nicht so, als wäre es bequem.

Aufgaben

Führung

  • Du führst 3–5 Account Manager:innen fachlich und disziplinarisch.
  • Du führst wöchentliche 1:1s nach klarer Struktur (Fortschritt / Probleme / Pläne) und verantwortest die Gesundheit deines Teams.
  • Du entwickelst deine Leute aktiv weiter — Schulungen, Feedback, strukturierte Einarbeitung.

Kunden

  • Du verantwortest Entwicklung und Ergebnis deines eigenen Kundenportfolios (Richtwert 6–8 Accounts, ausschließlich unsere anspruchsvollsten Kunden). Das Tagesgeschäft liegt bei deinen AMs.
  • Du bist geschätzter Ansprechpartner auf der Senior-Entscheiderebene deiner Kunden und platzierst Themen aktiv in Kunden-Calls.
  • Du erkennst Churn-Risiken früh, entscheidest die Gegenmaßnahmen für dein Team und drehst gefährdete Accounts zurück in Wachstum.

Fachlichkeit & Prozesse

  • Du bist die fachliche Rückfallebene deines Teams — Klaviyo- und CRM-Architektur beherrschst du in der Breite.
  • Du coachst deine AMs fachlich und baust ihre Fähigkeiten auf, statt nur Fragen zu beantworten.
  • Du ownst einen unternehmensweiten Prozess rund um unsere Mitarbeitenden (z. B. Onboarding oder Offboarding).
  • Du stimmst Standards mit den anderen Key Account Managern ab und teilst Learnings aktiv.

Qualifikation

  1. Mindestens 3–4 Jahre Erfahrung im E-Mail-Marketing oder CRM; davon idealerweise ein Teil in einer Agentur oder im E-Commerce.
  2. Tiefe Praxis in Klaviyo oder einem vergleichbaren System (Braze, Emarsys, Bloomreach, Salesforce Marketing Cloud). Du hast komplexe Set-ups selbst gebaut, nicht nur begleitet.
  3. Erste Führungs- oder Mentoring-Erfahrung— du hast schon einmal Verantwortung für die Arbeit anderer getragen. Das muss nicht disziplinarisch gewesen sein.
  4. Sicherheit im Kundenkontakt auf Entscheiderebene— du hast schon mit Geschäftsführung oder Marketingleitung auf Augenhöhe gesprochen.
  5. Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau und gutes Englisch, schriftlich wie mündlich.
  6. Wohnsitz in Deutschland(steuer- und sozialversicherungsrechtlich zwingend).

Und was wir uns wünschen, aber nicht voraussetzen: Du gibst Feedback direkt und nimmst es genauso an. Du fragst nach dem Warum hinter den Zahlen eines Kunden. Du wartest nicht, bis dir jemand einen Prozess gibt.

Das ist nichts für dich, wenn …

  • … du Führung als Beförderung siehst und nicht als eigenes Handwerk, das man lernen muss.
  • … du Dinge lieber selbst machst, als sie abzugeben und jemanden dabei besser zu machen.
  • … du eine fertige Struktur erwartest. Wir bauen sie gerade — mit dir.
  • … du unangenehme Gespräche aufschiebst. Ein Teil dieser Rolle besteht daraus.
  • … du im Homeoffice Struktur von außen brauchst. Wir arbeiten vollständig remote.

Benefits

  • Ein Team, das dir gehört — und die Freiheit, es zu formen.
  • Klarheit über deinen eigenen Weg: Wir haben eine ausformulierte Level-Matrix. Du siehst schwarz auf weiß, was auf deinem Level erwartet wird und was der nächste Schritt ist.
  • Halbjährliche Entwicklungsgespräche mit echtem Feedback statt Formularen. Gehalt wird bei uns nach System vergeben, nicht nach Verhandlungsgeschick.
  • Führungskräfte-Ausbildung mit einem externen Coach, der Führungsteams bei Meta und in mehreren Scale-ups aufgebaut hat.
  • 100 % remote, überall in Deutschland — plus regelmäßige Team-Offsites und Workations.
  • MacBook, bei Bedarf zusätzliche Hardware.
  • 50 € monatliche Sachbezugskarte nach der Probezeit.

Sechs Sätze, an denen wir uns messen lassen — auch als Führungskraft:

Be confident.

We don't need all the answers to start, just the grit to find them first.

Be curious.

Let's be obsessed to find the ‚Why‘ to unlock the ‚How‘.

Keep growing.

Treat yourself like brilliant software: ship a new upgrade every month.

Be accountable.

Openness over cosiness. We own our words.

Act entrepreneurial.

Don't just do tasks: own real business impact.

Over-deliver where it matters.

Promise what's possible. Then challenge these boundaries.

We are a small, high-performing team that owns the operational systems, practices, and cross-functional coordination that enable 15+ product teams to deliver meaningful digital assessment experiences to millions of students and educators every year. We partner closely with Product, Technology, Design, and go-to-market functions, and we hold ourselves to the same bar we help others reach: rigorous, data-informed, and always improving.

Together, we are transforming College Board’s trusted assessment platform into a next generation digital assessment experience that is secure, user-centered, and built to evolve with the future of learning and assessment.

About the Opportunity

As Director, Analytics & Business Intelligence, you are the measurement infrastructure behind how Digital Product Operations understands and improves its impact. You build the dashboards, define the metrics, and create the coaching conditions that let product teams and the ProdOps function itself operate on evidence rather than instinct. You're comfortable building in a still-forming space, defining what "healthy" and "adopted" look like before anyone else has, and you don't stop at delivering a dashboard: you take a position on what the data means and own driving the change that follows.

In this role, you own the evidence layer that tells Digital Product whether it is improving, not just whether it is busy. Your work spans three domains at once: the health of 15+ product teams' planning and delivery practices, tracked through measures like roadmap completeness and Productboard field discipline; how well those teams are adopting ProdOps-driven ways of working; and whether the ProdOps function’s own change management efforts are gaining traction or falling short. You make the call on what the data means and what should happen next, then act on it, from diagnosing why an initiative is underperforming to designing and driving the intervention. You keep the Senior Director informed as a thought partner in that process, not a gatekeeper for it. What you build doesn’t wait to become useful until it reaches the Senior Director. Your dashboards, frameworks, and coaching directly change how product teams plan, prioritize, and improve.

In this role, you will:

Product Metrics & Dashboard Development (40%)

  • Define and build product metrics dashboards tracking roadmap maturity, Productboard field completeness, and roadmap change patterns across all 15+ Digital Product teams

  • Partner with Product leaders and PM/POs to define what “healthy” looks like for each metric, establishing baselines and targets that reflect meaningful improvement, not just activity

  • Design dashboards that are self-serve and easy to interpret, so product teams can understand their own health data without requiring ProdOps to translate it for them

  • Prepare executive-ready dashboards with minimal oversight from the Senior Director

  • Identify gaps in available data and partner with the Planning & Tooling Governance Director to ensure tooling standards support the metrics the function needs to track

ProdOps Effectiveness & Change Management Measurement (30%)

  • Build and maintain a measurement framework that tracks how effectively the product group is adopting ProdOps-driven ways of working, including new planning practices, tooling standards, and process changes

  • Define adoption metrics for each major ProdOps initiative before it launches, establishing what “adopted” looks like and how it will be measured from day one

  • Take a documented position on what the adoption data means, not just what it shows: diagnose whether gaps in adoption stem from awareness, capability, process design, or resistance, then bring a recommended course of action to the relevant stakeholders, partner with the relevant director to design the response, and own the follow-through to confirm whether the intervention worked

  • Track change management signals across the product group: awareness rates, behavior change indicators, and the difference between leading and lagging adoption signals

Dashboard Maintenance & Data Governance (20%)

  • Own ongoing maintenance of all dashboards across product and ProdOps metrics, ensuring data is current, accurate, and trustworthy at all times

  • Establish governance standards for metric definitions, ensuring consistent interpretation across teams and preventing measurement drift as the organization evolves

  • Conduct regular audits of data quality; identify and address gaps, inconsistencies, or stale data before they surface in leadership reviews or team conversations

  • Partner with the Planning & Tooling Governance Director to ensure metric definitions align with tooling standards and that field governance decisions support accurate measurement

  • Document all metric definitions, calculation methods, and data sources in the ProdOps Info Hub so the measurement framework is transparent and maintainable

Metrics Coaching & Adoption (10%)

  • Coach PM/POs on how to read and act on their roadmap health dashboards, translating data signals into product decisions and planning adjustments they can make independently

  • Coach the ProdOps team on how to interpret function effectiveness metrics, helping the team understand what the data is telling them and where to focus improvement efforts

  • Design coaching approaches that build genuine data literacy, not just tool familiarity, so teams develop the capability to operate independently rather than depending on ProdOps for interpretation

  • Identify patterns in how teams are misreading or ignoring their metrics; surface these patterns to the Senior Director and the relevant director as input for targeted interventions

About You

To qualify for this role, you must have:

  • 5+ years of experience in product analytics, business intelligence, or data analysis within a digital product or technology organization

  • Experience measuring and driving organizational change: you understand the difference between awareness and behavior change, track both, and take ownership of designing and following through on the intervention when adoption stalls

  • Comfort operating with ambiguity, defining what to measure and how for a function still establishing its own ways of working

  • Demonstrated experience building dashboards and metrics frameworks that teams actually use, not just technically sound, but genuinely adopted and acted on

  • Strong understanding of product management practices: you know what roadmap maturity, backlog health, and planning consistency look like in practice, and can design metrics that reflect them accurately

  • Strong data governance instincts: you define metrics precisely, document them clearly, and prevent measurement drift over time

  • Familiarity with Productboard, Jira, and Confluence as data sources: you know how to extract meaningful signals from product management tooling

  • Comfort with SQL and APIs to extract and validate your own data, even if you're not a technical builder yourself

  • Strong coaching and communication skills: you can translate data into clear, actionable guidance for non-technical audiences without losing accuracy

  • The ability to travel 5-7 times a year to College Board offices or on behalf of College Board business

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work

  • Authorization to work in the United States for any employer

  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.

  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal

  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input

  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking

  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success

About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.

  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise such as live coding, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than just a paycheck—we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation, grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.

A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $88,000 - $145,000.

  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at College Board.

  • We aim to make our best offer upfront—rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.

  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You’ll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it’s like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more.

jobs.excerpt: About the Company Launched in 2018, OI Infusion aims to improve the patient and provider experience while simultaneously lowering costs for both providers and payers.
jobs.description:
About the Company


Launched in 2018, OI Infusion aims to improve the patient and provider experience while simultaneously lowering costs for both providers and payers. The company operates both an infusion management service organization (MSO) and a network of multi-site ambulatory specialty infusion centers, called Novella. The MSO business line offers services such as staffing, managing operations, and revenue cycle operations for physician practices, enabling the specialty groups to provide infusion services to their patient base. We help our partners treat their patients in a comfortable, convenient, and affordable setting. The Novella ambulatory specialty infusion centers allow business to contract directly with payers and are a major lever for future growth. Since its inception, Novella has scaled to operate over 35 clinics in the New England region.

Position Summary

The Clinical Review Pharmacist is the quality gate that ensures every infusion order is clinically appropriate, payer-compliant, and accurately documented before authorization is requested. This role goes beyond medical necessity review: it requires payer policy literacy, sharp attention to detail, proactive case-building for complex and off-label therapies, and hands-on ownership of the denial response process from root-cause analysis through appeal or peer-to-peer support.

The right candidate does not simply check boxes against a policy database. They read the full clinical picture, anticipate payer pushback before submission, communicate clearly and specifically with sites and navigators about what is needed and why, and — when a denial occurs — build an airtight case to overturn it rather than placing the burden entirely on the referring provider

Salary: $100k-$130k.
Locatio: Remote

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Conduct thorough medical necessity review of infusion orders for both commercial and government payers across all designated drug therapies, applying the correct payer-specific medical policy for each case

  • Review the full patient chart to determine whether the patient meets payer criteria, including diagnosis, step therapy requirements, lab values, dosing, and continuation-of-therapy documentation

  • Maintain and actively use the PGR policy database as the primary source of truth; flag and update policy changes on a quarterly basis in coordination with the Director of RCM

  • Apply consistent, templated communication standards when PGR review results in a required action by the site, navigator, or provider.

  • Review and verify that each order is correctly dosed flagging dosing discrepancies with ordering providers before moving forward

  • When auth denials are received, work with intake leaders to write specifically tailored LMN to overturn the decision when necessary

  • Assist the intake team reviewing auth denials with clinical guidance and how to best proceed

  • Collaborate with clinical operations team on review and maintenance of order sets and drug preparation sheets to ensure clinical accuracy

  • Experience in navigating a fast-paced, high-volume environment with competing priorities and evolving payer landscapes

Minimum Qualifications

  • Minimum 2 years of infusion therapy experience preferred- Hospital, home health, etc.

  • Proficient with Microsoft suite- Word, Excel, Outlook

  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple tasks

  • Bachelor of Pharmacy or a Doctor of Pharmacy preferred

  • Be a pharmacist a current/clear license within the state

  • Minimum of four years of infusion pharmacy experience as a pharmacist preferred

  • Experience with providing clinical education and support for specialty medications

  • Clinical education and support for specialty medications is a plus

  • Thrives working in a fast pace working environment

Physical Demands and Work Environment

While performing the duties of this position, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to use hands or fingers, handle or feel objects, tools, or controls. The employee is occasionally required to stand; walk; sit; and reach with hands and arms. Specific vision abilities required by this position include close vision, distance vision, and the ability to adjust focus. The noise level in the work environment is usually low to moderate.

jobs.description:
Chief Growth Officer — CXM Group Crypto Exchange

Fully remote (EU timezone preferred) · Reports to Crypto Exchange CEO (interim: Group CEO) · Owns the growth function end-to-end

The liquidity problem is already solved — what doesn't exist yet is the growth playbook, and this role owns it from day one.

Most exchange growth mandates ask you to spend your first year chasing liquidity, convincing partners the product is real, and waiting for infrastructure to catch up to your ambitions. This one is different. CXM Group's retail centralised exchange is already live. Liquidity is sourced via prime exchanges. An established IB network — built through the group's existing multi-asset broker business — is primed for crypto activation. The blank sheet isn't the product. It's the acquisition playbook, and that's yours to write.

The primary bet is declared: IB-referred spot and perps trading as the lead acquisition channel, with CFD client conversion as a second-phase lever once the flywheel is turning. Your mandate is to confirm that hypothesis — through structured pilots with real stopping rules — or replace it. If it holds, you scale. Either way, you make the call on data.

This is a hands-on distribution role at the strategic level. In the early phase, you personally close the anchor IB relationships that validate the referral model. You equip country managers to activate their markets. You translate what IBs and customers are actually responding to — fee sensitivity, onboarding friction, product gaps — into clean demand signal for the CEO's roadmap decisions. The upside is tied directly to exchange growth performance.

Why this beats the seat you're in now

  • You inherit the starting line most growth leads spend a year reaching. Live product, sourced liquidity, a warm IB network — the infrastructure problems are solved before you arrive.
    - The hypothesis is declared, not vague. You're not walking into "figure out growth." You're validating a specific channel bet, with a clear timeline and the authority to kill it if the data says to.
    - The distribution network is warm, not cold. Existing IBs already have relationships with CXM Group. Crypto activation is an extension, not a cold start.
    - A CFD conversion pool you don't have to build. An established base of CFD traders with natural appetite for spot and perps exists as a Phase 2 channel — ready when the primary flywheel is turning.
    - Downside capped by group infrastructure. You operate under the regulatory, operational, and financial umbrella of an established multi-asset group. The execution risk is yours; the existential risk is not.
    - Compensation reflects the upside. Base salary, profit share tied directly to CEX growth performance, and a cross-referral incentive for directing clients across CXM Group divisions.

This is for you if

  • You've personally built or activated an IB or partner network — not inherited one — and you've closed the anchor relationships that made it move.
    - You've run structured acquisition pilots with real hypotheses and real stopping rules, and you're comfortable being the one who kills a bet, including your own.
    - You understand CEX mechanics — spot, perps, order book, onboarding economics — well enough to translate IB and customer feedback into product input without a translator.
    - You're currently a VP or Head of Growth, Partnerships, or IB Networks at a retail CEX, forex, or CFD platform and you've outgrown what the role can actually give you.
    - You can drive outcomes in a structure where you own the growth motion but not the P&L — and you know the difference between noise and a clean signal worth escalating to a CEO.
    - You want a seat close enough to the top that your judgment shapes the business, not just your team's targets.

Your first year

The first phase is immediate and personal. You identify and close the anchor IB partners whose activation sets the standard for everything that follows — this is hands-on relationship work, not delegation. In parallel, you equip country managers with the tools, commission structures, and product knowledge to run activation in their markets. By Q4 2026, you've run a structured pilot programme, read the cohort data, and made a clear call: the primary channel hypothesis holds and you shift to scale mode, or it doesn't and you redirect resources. Either outcome moves the business forward. If the hypothesis is confirmed, Phase 2 opens: activating the existing CFD client base as a conversion channel into spot and perps, with the IB infrastructure already beneath it. Throughout, you're the demand-signal function for the CEO — translating what the market is actually telling you into decisions about fees, product, and sequencing.

The ask

If this is the mandate you've been waiting for, tell us in a few lines: what's the first thing you'd want to know about the existing IB network before deciding how to activate it?

jobs.description:
Overview

Lynker Corporation is a leading provider of innovative solutions in weather and climate science. With a commitment to excellence and a passion for innovation, Lynker leverages cutting-edge technologies and scientific expertise to support the creation and delivery of improved operational weather forecasts. As part of our ongoing growth and expansion, we are seeking a dynamic and experienced Senior Wetlands Scientist to join our growing team.

Mapping wetlands accurately across large areas is hard, and the maps are only as trustworthy as the validation behind them. We are hiring a Senior Wetland Scientist to lead that work, combining wetland science, remote sensing, and cloud-native geospatial computing to produce defensible wetland products across regional to national extents. The role spans model development, large-area production, validation and uncertainty, and technical leadership.

You will sit close to our modeling and geospatial teams, turning wetlands science into methods that run reliably over large areas. The strongest candidates pair wetland and ecological expertise with strong geospatial and coding skills, and are comfortable moving between the underlying science, the data pipeline, and validation of the resulting maps.

Responsibilities

Duties of the Senior Wetlands Scientist will include the following:

  • Mapping at scale: produce, improve, and maintain versioned wetland maps across large regional to national extents.
  • Cloud-native geospatial: build and run mapping and modeling workflows using cloud-native geospatial tools, formats, and storage.
  • Wetland modeling: implement, adapt, and improve existing and new models for wetland potential and for wetland boundary and extent.
  • Data integration: integrate LiDAR-derived elevation, hydrology, imagery, soils, and existing wetland inventories into reproducible modeling pipelines.
  • Validation & QA: design validation against reference data, quantify uncertainty, and quality-control wetland maps for accuracy and consistency.
  • Communication: document methods and results, contribute to reports and proposals, and partner with the Platform, Modeling, and Applications teams that scale and serve your products.

Qualifications

The Senior Wetlands Scientist selected should have the following:

  • Master's or PhD in wetland science, ecology, geography, environmental or earth science, hydrology, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Roughly 5+ years of relevant experience, or a PhD plus a few years of relevant work.
  • Demonstrated experience mapping wetlands, land cover, or comparable features at large spatial scale.
  • Hands-on experience with cloud-native geospatial tooling, formats, and workflows.
  • Experience implementing or adapting geospatial or ecological models (wetland potential, habitat, boundary and extent, or comparable).
  • Proficiency in Python and/or R for geospatial analysis, with sound coding and reproducibility practices.

The Ideal Senior Wetlands Scientist will have the following:

  • Experience with wetland potential or probability modeling and with wetland delineation, boundary, and extent methods.
  • Experience applying machine learning to land-cover or wetland classification.
  • Familiarity with national wetland, hydrography, soils, and elevation datasets, and with remote-sensing inputs.
  • Experience with distributed or parallel processing for large-area geospatial work (e.g., cloud batch, Dask, or Google Earth Engine).
  • A record of scientific publication or successful proposal work.
  • Colorado Front Range presence for periodic in-person collaboration.

Lynker is a growing, employee owned business, specializing in professional, scientific and technical services. Our continually expanding team combines scientific expertise with mature, results-driven processes and tools to achieve technically sound, cost effective solutions in hydrology/water sciences, geospatial analysis, information technology, resource management, conservation, and management and business process improvement.

About NetDocuments

At NetDocuments, we're shaping the future of legal work. We believe legal professionals should spend less time searching for information and managing documents, and more time solving complex problems, serving clients, and delivering meaningful outcomes. That's why we're building technology that helps organizations work smarter, collaborate more effectively, and unlock the full value of their institutional knowledge.

Our team is redefining what's possible for legal technology. NetDocuments is the trusted intelligent document management platform for legal professionals and the company behind the industry's first and only legal context graph—a breakthrough that gives legal professionals and AI a richer understanding of how matters, documents, people, and knowledge connect across an organization while respecting enterprise-grade security, governance, permissions, and ethical walls.

Innovation is only part of our story. We believe our greatest strength is our people. We foster a collaborative, inclusive, and high-performing culture where curiosity is encouraged, diverse perspectives are valued, and employees are empowered to make a meaningful impact. Whether you're building products, serving customers, or supporting the business, your work helps shape the future of one of the world's most trusted legal technology platforms.

That commitment to our employees and customers has earned us recognition as one of the nation's top workplaces, including:

  • Four consecutive appearances on the Inc. 5000 list of America's Fastest-Growing Private Companies
  • Five-time Top Workplace USA winner
  • Five-time Salt Lake Tribune Top Workplace

If you're excited to solve meaningful challenges, work alongside talented colleagues, and help define the next generation of legal technology, we'd love to meet you.

What You’ll Do

At NetDocuments, we’re shaping the future of how legal professionals harness the power of AI to work smarter, faster, and with greater confidence. We’re looking for a dynamic Senior Product Manager to join our team and help define, build, and deliver intelligent solutions that transform the way our customers interact with their information. In this role, you’ll collaborate with leaders across product, engineering, and design to bring innovative ideas to life—turning customer insights and emerging AI capabilities into real-world impact. If you’re excited by the challenge of driving product excellence in a rapidly evolving space, this is the opportunity to make your mark.

You will:

  • Collaborate with leadership to define and drive the roadmap for AI-powered solutions, assessing new product ideas and enhancements.

  • Partner with stakeholders across the organization and among our customer base to collect feedback, validate ideas, and set priorities.
  • Analyze customer feedback, usage metrics, and other data to inform iterative improvements to the product.
